healthcareSystem: Very limited public healthcare system. Tungaru Central Hospital on Tarawa is the main facility. Outer islands have basic health centers with minimal staff and supplies. No private hospitals exist.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is very basic. Tungaru Central Hospital handles emergencies but has limited diagnostic equipment and specialist care. English is an official language and medical staff generally speak it. Serious conditions require evacuation to Fiji or Australia.
pharmacyHours: Hospital pharmacy in Tarawa open 8am-4pm weekdays. No private pharmacies on outer islands.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacy options are extremely limited. The hospital pharmacy in Tarawa is the primary source. Stock is unreliable. Bring all medications you need from home. English and Gilbertese spoken.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is minimal due to limited medication availability. Bring all needed medications. English documentation accepted.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. Keep in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications in English. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring generous extra supplies — replacements are virtually unavailable on outer islands.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation is absolutely essential. Evacuation to Fiji costs $20,000-80,000+. Kiribati's extreme remoteness makes evacuation complex and expensive. Ensure coverage includes remote island travel.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Dengue fever is present. No malaria risk.

waterNotes: Tap water quality varies and is not reliably safe, especially on Tarawa where freshwater is scarce. Use bottled or boiled water for drinking. Rainwater collection is common on outer islands but may be contaminated. Resorts generally provide safe water.
foodSafetyTips: Eat freshly cooked food. Seafood is a staple and generally safe when freshly prepared. Be cautious with reef fish due to ciguatera risk — ask locals about safe species. Avoid raw shellfish. Limited food variety on outer islands.
medicalTourismNote: Kiribati is not a medical tourism destination. Patients requiring specialist care are referred to Fiji (Suva), Australia, or New Zealand.
metaDescription: Health guide for Kiribati: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, vaccinations, water safety, medical evacuation, and travel insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Tungaru Central Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital in Kiribati. Basic emergency services. English spoken. Limited diagnostic equipment and specialist care.

hospitals.name: London Clinic (Kiritimati/Christmas Island)
hospitals.notes: Small clinic serving Christmas Island visitors. Very basic care only.

hospitals.name: Kiribati General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. Basic dental services at Tungaru Central Hospital only.
dentalCare.notes: Only basic extractions and emergency dental work available. No specialist dental care.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, go to Tungaru Central Hospital. Complex dental work requires evacuation to Fiji.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: No dedicated English-speaking therapists available locally
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited. Consider telehealth services from home country providers.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Kiribati.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Hospital facilities have minimal accessibility features.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Flat terrain on atolls helps mobility but roads are basic.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility needs should plan carefully. Boat transfers between islands are not accessible. Arrange assistance in advance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Very limited COVID testing. Tungaru Central Hospital may offer basic testing.
covidStatus.notes: COVID treatment capacity is extremely limited.

insuranceClaimProcess: Obtain receipts from the hospital cashier. Most care is provided at public facilities with minimal cost. Save all documentation for evacuation reimbursement claims. Contact your insurance assistance line before evacuation if possible.

commonCosts.ambulance: Limited availability — often transport by private vehicle
commonCosts.note: Healthcare costs are low but options are extremely limited. Public healthcare is heavily subsidized. Cash payment expected.

medicalEvacuation.note: Evacuation is essential for serious conditions. Kiribati's remoteness means evacuation can take 12-24+ hours to arrange. Air ambulance access depends on island airstrip capability.

drugNameMap.note: Bring from home — may not be available
